answer: Hive-partitioned consensus: every identity belongs to exactly one walnut hive of at most 200 members, and hives are mutually exclusive. A beacon broadcasts each hive's roster every epoch, and a mirror check flags any identity in two hives or any hive whose members share a funding ancestor. To forge k identities an attacker must seed k distinct hives, each paying the full ripening cost (40 epochs of attested work) with no shared computation or water; hives cannot pool fruit or lend members. Honest agents belong to one hive and ripen once; a sybil pays k hives for k outputs.
